international.title: Smoke seen from a mile away as army detonates US stockpile of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
international.summary: Controlled blast to dispose of lead azide risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in 100-mile radius The US army detonated the nation’s entire stockpile of the the bomb-making material lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning, despite an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects. The controlled blast, which took place at about 10.00am ET, was to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the chemical that was stored at the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa that is home to about 400 people.
